title: PolicyHandshake
description: The two messages that open a policy worker session (ADR-010 §2, ADR-008 §3). The client sends hello with the contracts it speaks; the worker answers ready with its own set plus its encoder version, the hash of the engine-data table it was built with and the ids of the checkpoints it loaded. Any difference refuses the session before a battle starts.

ContractVersion.description: One contract the two sides must agree on: its name, schema_version and the SHA-256 of its schema file's JCS bytes.

schema_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the contract schema's JCS bytes: lowercase hex.

Checkpoint.description: A loaded checkpoint: its role and id (the SHA-256 of its safetensors file bytes).

FeatureSetStatement.description: A candidate feature set by name and identity hash (CandidateFeatures.feature_set and feature_set_hash).

Hello.description: Client to worker: the contracts the client speaks.

contracts.description: Sorted by name, no name twice (a reader rule).

inference.description: The batching the client expects (a training self-play client of a run whose config sets generation.inference). Omitted means batch 1. The worker refuses the session if its own batching differs, and the client refuses a ready that states another.

Ready.description: Worker to client: its contracts and what it loaded.

contracts.description: Sorted by name, no name twice (a reader rule).

encoder_version.description: The encoder the worker reads observations with.

engine_data_hash.description: SHA-256 of the engine-data table (EngineData JCS bytes) the encoder's vocabularies come from.

checkpoints.description: Sorted by role, each role once (a reader rule).

feature_set.description: The candidate feature set the worker's checkpoints need (ADR-022 section 3): omitted when they need none. The client refuses the session if it cannot supply exactly this set, and attaches candidate_features to a query only for a worker that states one.

opponent_sheet.description: The opponent sheet source the worker's checkpoints need (ADR-027 slice 4): omitted when they need none. feature_set is opponent-sheet/1 and feature_set_hash the feature set hash the block's source.hash must equal. The client refuses the session if it cannot supply exactly this source, and attaches opponent_sheet to a query only for a worker that states one.

value_query.description: True when the worker answers value queries (PolicyQuery sampling kind value): its checkpoints' encoder layout does not fill any token or field column from candidate_features arrays or opponent_sheet, so the value head needs no candidate rows (ADR-026 erratum E2 decision 7). Omitted otherwise, and then a value query is refused.

inference.description: The batching the worker was started with: omitted for batch 1. The client refuses a ready whose batching is not the one its hello asked for.

Inference.description: The batching of the worker's forward pass (ADR-028 section 2, #1195): up to max_batch queued queries are scored in one padded forward pass on the CPU. Absent means batch 1, which is what every evaluation, sealed and head-to-head path asks for.
